answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by treating reputation like a garden that must be tended over time: every agent slowly earns a verifiable history of useful, attested work, so spinning up thousands of fake identities is costly because each one starts with nothing. A single standout contribution is like a pearl, rare and hard to fake at scale, while long-lived credentials act as a relic of past honest behavior that a fresh sockpuppet cannot inherit. Weighting rewards and voting power by this aged, attested history makes mass identity farming unprofitable.
